Prepare data for a provider model

Source: R/data_pp_data.R
pp_data.Rd

Checks and arranges the data every model and test in the package reads: the outcome, the covariates, the provider identifier and, when the data have repeated observations, the patient identifier and the number of trials; for a survival outcome the time, event and entry columns. Rows are sorted by provider and patient, provider sizes are counted, and providers below the size cutoff or with no or all events are flagged.

Usage

pp_data(
  data,
  y = NULL,
  x,
  provider,
  patient = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  event = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  outcome = c("auto", "binary", "binomial", "continuous", "survival"),
  cutoff = 10,
  check = TRUE,
  message = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

a data frame.

y

name of the outcome column: 0/1 for a binary outcome, the number of events out of n trials for a binomial outcome, or any numeric value for a continuous outcome. NULL for a survival outcome, which is given by time and event.

x

names of the covariate columns. Covariates must be numeric; code factors as 0/1 columns first.

provider

name of the provider identifier column.

patient

name of the patient identifier column, or NULL when every row is an independent unit. Required by the patient-clustered tests.

n

name of the column with the number of trials per row (binomial outcome), or NULL.

time, event

for a survival outcome, the names of the columns with the end of each row's at-risk interval and its 0/1 event indicator.

start

optional name of the column with the start of the at-risk interval (left truncation or counting-process rows); 0 when NULL.

weights

optional name of a column of positive case weights, used by fit_cox().

offset

optional name of a column with a known term of the linear predictor, used by fit_cox().

outcome

"auto" (default), "binary", "binomial", "continuous" or "survival". With "auto" the outcome is survival when time or event is given, binomial when n is given, binary when every value of y is 0 or 1, and continuous otherwise.

cutoff

providers with fewer than cutoff patients (rows when patient is NULL) are kept in the data but marked included = FALSE and left out of model fitting. Default 10. Use 0 to fit every provider, as the two-stage survival models of the KECC measures do, and select the providers to report at the test stage.

check

run pp_check() first (missing values and zero-variance covariates are errors; near-zero variance, high correlation and large VIF are warnings). Default TRUE.

message

print a short summary. Default TRUE.

Value

An object of class pp_data: a list with

data

the sorted data frame with the named columns plus the logical columns included, no_events and all_events (the last two are FALSE for a continuous outcome, and all_events for a survival outcome).

vars

the column names y, x, provider, patient, n, time, start, event, weights, offset and the outcome type.

sizes

one row per provider in the sorted order: provider, rows, patients (NA without a patient column), included, no_events, all_events.

cutoff

the cutoff used.

Details

Rows are ordered by provider, then patient, with order()'s radix method, which sorts character identifiers in the C locale and is stable: a patient's rows keep their input order, so sort the data by time within patient first when the stabilized tests will be used. Provider identifiers are converted to character.

Only the named columns are kept.

See also

pp_check(), sim_kecc()

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", cutoff = 10, message = FALSE)
pd
#> Prepared data: 2679 rows, 20 providers, 759 patients
#>   outcome y (binary); 3 covariates
#>   20 providers with at least 10 patients included; 0 excluded
#>   included providers with no events: 0; with all events: 0
#>   event rate among included rows: 25.2%
head(pd$sizes)
#>   provider rows patients included no_events all_events
#> 1     P001   64       18     TRUE     FALSE      FALSE
#> 2     P002  197       53     TRUE     FALSE      FALSE
#> 3     P003   45       15     TRUE     FALSE      FALSE
#> 4     P004  164       48     TRUE     FALSE      FALSE
#> 5     P005  122       37     TRUE     FALSE      FALSE
#> 6     P006  208       57     TRUE     FALSE      FALSE

s <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, type = "survival", seed = 1)
ps <- pp_data(s, x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", time = "stop", start = "start",
              event = "event", cutoff = 0, message = FALSE)
ps
#> Prepared data: 2679 rows, 20 providers, 759 patients
#>   survival outcome: time stop from start, event event; 3 covariates
#>   20 providers with at least 0 patients included; 0 excluded
#>   included providers with no events: 0
#>   events among included rows: 336 (12.5% of rows)
